misconceptions.description: Student marks nodes as visited when DEQUEUING instead of when ENQUEUING, causing duplicates
observable_patterns: Marks visited inside while loop after dequeue
Same node enqueued multiple times before processing
misconceptions.invariant: Mark a node visited WHEN YOU ENQUEUE IT, not when you dequeue it. This prevents the same node being added to the queue multiple times.

transfer_templates.question:
Graph: 0-1, 0-2, 1-2 (triangle). BFS from 0.
If you mark visited when DEQUEUING:
- Queue: [0]
- Dequeue 0, enqueue 1, 2. Queue: [1, 2]
- Dequeue 1, enqueue 2 (not marked yet!). Queue: [2, 2]
What happens? How does marking when ENQUEUING fix this?
transfer_templates.target_reasoning: Node 2 is enqueued twice. If marked visited when enqueued: after enqueueing 2 from node 0, it's marked visited. When processing node 1, 2 is already visited — skip.

misconceptions.description: Student omits visited tracking in DFS, causing infinite loops on cyclic graphs
observable_patterns: DFS without a visited set or boolean array
misconceptions.invariant: Every DFS on a graph (not tree) must track visited nodes to avoid infinite loops on cycles.

transfer_templates.question:
Graph: 0-1, 1-2, 2-0 (cycle). DFS from 0 without visited tracking.
Trace the execution. Does it terminate?
transfer_templates.target_reasoning: Without visited: 0→1→2→0→1→2→... infinite loop. With visited set: mark 0, go to 1, mark 1, go to 2, mark 2, try 0 (visited), backtrack. Terminates.
